descripcion: At B2 the goal is to replace the most overused words — very, good, bad, nice, a lot — with one clearer alternative each time. The full ten-word ban used at C1 isn't the target yet; picking a better word for the five most common offenders is enough.

filas: plenty, a fair amount, a number

ejemplos.texto: It was exhausting, not just tiring.
The service was thorough and professional.
There's a fair amount of work left to do.

notas: Very plus an adjective usually means there's a single stronger word available instead.
Good and bad need a follow-up question: good in what way? — the answer is usually the better word.
Thing is almost always avoidable and worth replacing with the actual noun.

contraste.es: Spanish relies on muy + adjective just as English relies on very, so the habit transfers directly. The fix is the same in both languages: a stronger single word (exhausted rather than very tired).
contraste.de: German sehr + adjective works exactly like very + adjective, and German has the same stronger single words (erschöpft – exhausted). The habit and the fix both transfer directly.
contraste.it: Italian often intensifies with -issimo (stanchissimo), which becomes very tired. English prefers a stronger single word: exhausted.
contraste.fr: French très + adjective works like very + adjective, and French has the same stronger single words (épuisé – exhausted). The habit and the fix both transfer directly.
contraste.pt: Portuguese intensifies with muito or -íssimo (cansadíssimo), which becomes very tired. English prefers a stronger single word: exhausted.

errores: Overusing very where a single stronger adjective exists.
Using thing repeatedly instead of naming the object.
Replacing an overused word with one that's too obscure for the context.
autochequeo: Have I replaced very + adjective with a single stronger word at least twice?
Have I avoided thing where a specific noun would work?
Are good and bad replaced with more precise words?
Is the replacement word appropriate for the register, not too obscure?
Have I used at least five precise adjectives overall?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on lexical precision. Flag every very + adjective, every good/bad, and every thing that could be replaced with something more specific. Do not rewrite the text.
